npcdata/094.edt: You are new around here. I am Vasko, I keep an eye on the square.
Back again? The square has not moved since you left.
Fine weather for walking, if you like dust.
Every road out of here leads to more dust.
I have no use for that.
Ask a clear question and you get a clear answer.
Threats do not frighten an old man with nothing to lose.
I am too old to carry a rifle for you.
Go well.
Enough talk. Leave me be.
Strangers with guns usually mean trouble for the square.
Still, you look like you can keep your word.
You came back. Have you seen the old hermit yet?
The well water is sweeter since the rains came.
There is a hermit in the hills nobody has seen for a month.
If you find him, tell me he is alive.
Wait here. I want to show you something by the trees.
Follow me, quietly now.
From here you can see the path to the hills. That is where he went.
That is all you get from me today.
Tell me the truth: did the soldiers send you here?
Then I have nothing more to say to you.
Good. I did not think you were one of them.
You are lying, and you lie badly.
Perhaps you are telling the truth after all.
Spare rounds? My old pistol will thank you. I will keep them.
Money for the square. It will buy seed for the gardens.
Keep your pistol. I want no guns in my hands.
npcdata/065.edt: Haven't seen you in town before. The name is Marsh.
I keep my rifle oiled and my mouth shut.
Keep it, I have no use for that.
Ask what you came to ask.
Easy. Nobody needs to get hurt here.
I did some soldiering once. I might do some more, for the right people.
I'm no volunteer. Pay me every day and I'll follow you anywhere.
Word is the soldiers pulled out of the hills to the south.
Deal. Let me get my gear.
npcdata/123.edt: Please, are you going east? I need to get out of this town.
The road east is not safe for a woman alone.
My cousins keep a farm two valleys away.
I can't take that from you.
I only want to go home.
Please, I have done nothing to you!
I would only slow you down.
I have waited three weeks for someone to take me along.
Will you take me with you? I promise I won't slow you down.
Let's keep moving, I don't like it here.
Here? All right, I'll find my own way from here.
My cousins will feed you well if we ever get there.
npcdata/075.edt: So these are the ones who thought they could walk into my country.
Tell me who sent you, and do not waste my afternoon.
Honesty. How dull, and how useful.
Silence will not keep you comfortable for long.
A clumsy lie. My guards will teach you better ones.
Hm. Perhaps you are only fools after all.
That should loosen a tongue or two.
Wake them. I am not finished.
npcdata/135.edt: The guards will take them back to the cells, my lady.
I will see the yard is locked for the night.
npcdata/136.edt: It is over. She will never sign another order again.
The tunnels under the mines are still crawling. We cannot rest yet.
npcdata/137.edt: Then let the bells ring. The country is ours again.
npcdata/087.edt: Welcome to my club. Mind the sawdust, it hides the teeth.
You look like you can throw a punch. Want to try one of my lads in the ring?
The lads train every afternoon. The crowd only comes for blood.
Suit yourself. The ring will still be here tomorrow.
Step into the ring when you are ready. Fists only, and stay inside the ropes.
That is not boxing. Get out of my ring, the bout is off.
Bell! That is the end of it.
Now that is how it is done. The crowd will talk about this one.
You will feel that tomorrow. Come back when the swelling is gone.
npcdata/097.edt: You look like people who need a ride. I'm Hale. I fly, when they let me.
My bird is parked at the Drassen airstrip. The soldiers took my keys, not my skills.
Get me to the helipad in Drassen and I'll fly you anywhere the guns can't reach.
Walk me to Drassen? I'll stay behind you and keep my head down.
Keep moving. Every hour on the ground is an hour they could find us.
This isn't the airstrip. Drassen, remember? The big field with the hangar.
There she is. Give me a minute to check her over, then she's yours to call.
npcdata/106.edt: You chased the soldiers out? Then this mine works for you now. I'm Stroud, I run the crews.
The men dig harder when the pay comes on time.
Ore comes out of the hill, money goes into your account. That's the whole deal.
We need new timber for the props.
Half the crew is from the village down the road.
Lamp oil is the one thing we never have enough of.
Mind the carts on the rails.
The night shift starts at eight.
Water's rising in the lower gallery again.
We need new timber for the props.
Half the crew is from the village down the road.
Lamp oil is the one thing we never have enough of.
Mind the carts on the rails.
The night shift starts at eight.
Water's rising in the lower gallery again.
We need new timber for the props.
Half the crew is from the village down the road.
The vein is thinning out. A few more weeks and this hill is empty.
Something is loose in the tunnels! The crews won't go back down!
The night shift starts at eight.
Water's rising in the lower gallery again.
We need new timber for the props.
Half the crew is from the village down the road.

Mind the carts on the rails.
The night shift starts at eight.
They're back down there. We stopped digging until somebody deals with them.
The tunnels are quiet again. The crews went back to work this morning.

npcdata/147.edt: Garvey's. Guns in, guns out, no questions.
Business is slow since the soldiers came. Garvey remembers who helps.
Prices are on the wall. The wall doesn't haggle and neither do I.
npcdata/124.edt: Brandt's trading post. I buy anything that still works.
Business is slow since the soldiers came. Brandt remembers who helps.
Prices are on the wall. The wall doesn't haggle and neither do I.
npcdata/113.edt: Fuel, parts and the odd rifle. Quist, at your service.
Business is slow since the soldiers came. Quist remembers who helps.
Prices are on the wall. The wall doesn't haggle and neither do I.
npcdata/125.edt: Bandages, pills and a little hardware. Rook's pharmacy.
Business is slow since the soldiers came. Rook remembers who helps.
Prices are on the wall. The wall doesn't haggle and neither do I.
npcdata/126.edt: Solberg's. Ammunition by the box, if you have the money.
Business is slow since the soldiers came. Solberg remembers who helps.
Prices are on the wall. The wall doesn't haggle and neither do I.
npcdata/130.edt: Tamm. Bring it in broken, take it out working.
Business is slow since the soldiers came. Tamm remembers who helps.
Prices are on the wall. The wall doesn't haggle and neither do I.
npcdata/151.edt: Ulrik's bar. Drinks for the thirsty, and a few things under the counter.
Business is slow since the soldiers came. Ulrik remembers who helps.
Prices are on the wall. The wall doesn't haggle and neither do I.
npcdata/152.edt: Vale's shop. We stock what the convoys forget.
Business is slow since the soldiers came. Vale remembers who helps.
Prices are on the wall. The wall doesn't haggle and neither do I.
npcdata/154.edt: Wynn's canteen. Even in the capital people need to eat.
Business is slow since the soldiers came. Wynn remembers who helps.
Prices are on the wall. The wall doesn't haggle and neither do I.

npcdata/civ10.edt: Mind the potholes, nobody has fixed the road in years.
We get by. Some days better than others.
If you want work, there is none to be had here.
The well is that way. The water is warm but it is water.
My cousin keeps goats. I keep my distance from the goats.
Strangers come and go. The square stays the same.
You look tired. Everybody looks tired lately.
The market opens when the trucks come. They rarely come.
I would offer you tea, but we ran out of tea.
Do not believe what they say on the radio.
Walk carefully after dark, the dogs are not friendly.
The old church bell cracked last winter. Now it just clanks.
Everyone here knows everyone. Except you.
It rained on Tuesday. People are still talking about it.
Good day to you. Mostly good, anyway.
npcdata/civ11.edt: Is that a real gun? Can I hold it?
My brother says he is braver than you.
I can run faster than anybody on this street!
Mama says not to talk to strangers.
I saw a lizard as big as a cat this morning.
Are you a soldier? You do not look like a soldier.
We play football with a can. You can play too.
My dog only listens to me.
Why is your hat so funny?
I know a secret but I will not tell you.
The older kids took our ball again.
Can you climb that roof? I bet you cannot.
I am going to be a pilot one day.
npcdata/civ27.edt: Stay where you are and nobody gets hurt.
I just count the boxes, I do not want trouble.
Halt! Show me your papers. Any papers.
Somebody report this to the captain.
This post is off limits to you.
I have orders. I think I have orders.
You picked the wrong road, friend.
Do not make me call for help.
My shift ends in an hour. Wait an hour.
You are not on my list.
Hands where I can see them.
npcdata/civ37.edt: Lay down your weapons. You are outnumbered.
Give up now and you will live to see tomorrow.
There are too many of us. Surrender.
Drop the guns. Nobody else has to bleed today.
Your fight is over. Throw down your arms.
npcdata/civ06.edt: Another gun in town. That never ends well for us.
Leave us alone. We have had enough of armed men.
Whatever you are selling, nobody here is buying.
You say you help. They all said that.
The last group like you took our chickens.
I have nothing to say to you.
Every time someone comes to save us, we bury someone.
Trust is earned. You have earned none.
Do not drag our street into your war.
We remember faces. We will remember yours.
There is nothing left here worth fighting over.
npcdata/civ07.edt: My mother says you are trouble.
I am not scared of you. Not much.
We are not allowed to play outside anymore.
Your boots are muddy and so is your face.
Do not come near our house.
Papa hid the radio because of people like you.
